metadata.description: Single-plugin marketplace exposing the cc-enforcer discipline plugin.

plugins.name: cc-enforcer
plugins.description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls rather than asking it nicely. PreToolUse denies an edit before it lands — editing a file you never opened this session, a suppression marker with no adjacent why-comment, a hardcoded secret or user-home path, the fourth small patch to one file, a dangerous shell flag. A nine-layer Stop gate then refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the user's ORIGINAL request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight backed by a hook; "Imperial Edict" regexes you define per project; a repo-wide sync gate; CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the documentation cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, Linux + Windows CI, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.39.0 thins the injected contract, because it had been eating the feature it was supposed to leave room for. v0.38.3 fixed the symptom — edicts dropped silently on a long install path; this is the cause. The SessionStart contract had grown to 9,262 characters against a 10,000-character hook cap and nothing gated it: 991 characters of headroom at v0.29, 914 at v0.32, 552 at v0.35, by which point a real install path plus two real edicts no longer fit and a headline feature was degrading to nothing in the field. It is now 6,627 characters with 3,373 of headroom. What came out was duplication, not text: section 2's Recovery column, every word of which is printed at deny time in the block reason's own recovery section, and section 1's paragraph rows, whose heading already calls it a one-line index — each concept checked against prompts/user-prompt.md, re-injected EVERY turn, before being cut. Three tokens that lived only in the Recovery column were folded into the trigger cells rather than dropped. Three things the first pass cut that lived nowhere else at cold start went back in, caught by the tests that assert them: the four self-quiz questions verbatim and the layer (e) / layer (f) consequence for rules 08 and 09. The zh mirror got the same treatment, because a mirror that stops mirroring is how the deny set came to differ between languages in v0.26. The gate: a 120-character install root plus three edicts rendered by the real renderer must survive in both languages with no elision — ordinary parameters, named in the test, verified RED against the pre-thinning contract. 741 -> 742 tests. Prior — v0.38.3 fixes two defects found by verifying v0.38.2 the way it should be verified — cloning the remote into a fresh directory and running the suite there. Five tests failed while CI was green on the same commit on two platforms, which made 'verification artefact' the obvious conclusion; both were real. The clone sat at a 110-character path and this repository lives at a 23-character one. First: when the contract alone fills the 10,000-character hook cap, build_context dropped every edict and returned SILENTLY, so a session on a deeply-nested install was governed by rules it had never been shown and had no way to learn about — the v0.34.1 defect (all edicts elided, notice reporting 0) living in the sibling branch three releases after the class was supposedly closed. Reproduced first-party across install-root lengths before the fix; the branch now reports the count using the same counter _clip_edicts locates cut points with, because counting twice two ways is how the original notice came to disagree with its own clipper. Second: the header printed the install root twice, and the second copy came out of the budget the header exists to protect — naming it once takes a 300-character root from losing every edict to keeping them. Also a test that sliced the first 200 characters and asserted a filename was inside: true at a 23-character root, false at 110, so it failed on code that was working. It measures the header now. Both fixes verified RED against the pre-fix code, the elision fix with a twin so it cannot degenerate into 'always drop everything and report it'. 738 -> 741 tests (v0.38.3). Prior — v0.38.2 takes CLAUDE.md out of the repository. It is the project instruction file Claude Code loads — written for an agent rather than a reader, and its metadata section carries the maintainer's mail address and machine paths. Claude Code reads it from the working tree regardless of git, so untracking costs a local session nothing and a clone simply does not get one. Removing the file was the small half: it was load-bearing in fourteen places — four registered claims in the doc gate, the module-inventory tree, the Bash-deny surface list, the current-release narrative scan, six published links that would have 404'd on the front page, five more in the CHANGELOG, and the release checklist that both READMEs told contributors to go read there. The first attempt made each registry tolerate the file's absence and produced a suite that behaved one way locally and another on CI; that was replaced by a single rule — the doc gates scan the TRACKED repository, link resolution included, so a link to CLAUDE.md fails here exactly as it would in a clone even though the file is on this disk. Verified by running the gate in both states and getting identical results. The release checklist moved into both READMEs' Contributing sections in their own language; the CHANGELOG's references were de-linked but not de-worded, since rewriting what a dated entry says is the falsification the v0.33.0 rename entry refused. A new assertion holds both halves: out of the index AND ignored, because `git rm --cached` alone lets the next `git add -A` put it straight back. 737 -> 738 tests (v0.38.2). Full release history: CHANGELOG.md.
